description:
PER_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_PROPERTIES (src/backend.rs:103) lists 5 wire-name strings (keywords, color, freeBusyStatus, useDefaultAlerts, alerts). Of these, only useDefaultAlerts is a variant of the CalendarEventProperty enum (src/backend.rs:50). The docstring at backend.rs:99-102 notes this is deliberate because the four others — keywords, color, freeBusyStatus, alerts — are 'reserved as future additions but not yet enumerated'.

The hazard: when a future contributor adds CalendarEventProperty::Color (etc.), they have to remember TWO things stay in sync: the enum variant, and the wire-string const. The string-based is_per_user_calendar_event_property API does not type-check against the enum. A handler that routes per-user vs shared based on the enum (using a match) will silently miscategorize properties that exist in the const but not the enum — until somebody notices the bug in production via a corrupt shared-vs-per-user split.

Mitigation options for a future task:
  1. Add a doc-test or compile-fail test asserting that every variant of CalendarEventProperty whose Display/AsRef matches a string in PER_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_PROPERTIES is routed correctly.
  2. Add a single 'reserved for future' const PROPERTIES_NOT_YET_IN_ENUM = [...] alongside PER_USER so the gap is explicit, and assert PER_USER = ENUM_PER_USER ∪ PROPERTIES_NOT_YET_IN_ENUM via a test.
  3. Generate PER_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_PROPERTIES from the enum (impossible until all are variants).

Trigger condition: a backend implementor matches on CalendarEventProperty for patch routing, gets all-variants coverage from the compiler, and ships the bug because the missing variants flow through the wildcard arm.
File path: crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/backend.rs:99-120
title: calendars-types: PER_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_PROPERTIES drift hazard from CalendarEventProperty enum
